title: Set 32

sentences.ko: 여동생이 몇 달만 우리 집에 들어와 살겠다는데 내가 벌써 그래도 된다는 식으로 말해 버렸어. 이걸 어떻게 물러야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: My sister wants to move in with me for a few months, and I already said maybe. I don't know how to take that back.

alts.text: So my sister's asking to crash with me for a few months, and I already told her maybe. No idea how to walk that back.
My sister has asked to stay with me for a few months, and I have already told her it might be possible. I am not certain how to retract that.

sentences.note: **take that back**, **walk that back** 은 이미 한 말을 없던 걸로 물린다는 뜻입니다. **crash with me** 는 남의 집에 잠깐 얹혀 지낸다는 편한 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 삼 년은 됐지? 그동안 어떻게 지냈는지 얘기 좀 해 봐, 아직 포틀랜드에 살아?
sentences.text: It's got to be three years, right? So catch me up, are you still out in Portland?

alts.text: Three years, has to be. So fill me in, you still out in Portland?
It must be three years now, is that right? Please tell me what I have missed. Are you still living in Portland?

sentences.note: **catch me up**, **fill me in** 은 못 본 사이의 소식을 알려 달라는 말입니다. **out in Portland** 의 out 은 멀리 떨어진 동네에 산다는 느낌을 줍니다.

sentences.ko: 3월에 기타를 샀어. 한 이 주 동안은 매일 밤 쳤는데 그 뒤로는 계속 소파 뒤에 처박혀 있어.
sentences.text: I bought a guitar in March and played it every night for like two weeks, and it's been behind the couch ever since.

alts.text: Got myself a guitar back in March, played it every night for maybe two weeks, and it's been sitting behind the couch ever since.
I purchased a guitar in March and played it every evening for approximately two weeks. It has been behind the couch ever since.

sentences.note: **ever since** 는 그 일이 있고 나서 지금까지 죽 그렇다는 뜻입니다. **for like two weeks** 의 like 는 이 주쯤이라고 대충 말할 때 넣는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 점심 먹으려고 앉아서 영상 하나 틀었는데 정신 차려 보니 네 시였고 나는 남이 카펫 청소하는 걸 보고 있더라.
sentences.text: I sat down to eat lunch and put on one video, and then it's four o'clock and I'm watching people clean carpets.

alts.text: Sat down for lunch, put on one video, and next thing it's four o'clock and I'm watching people clean carpets.
I sat down to have lunch and started one video. Then it was four o'clock and I was watching people clean carpets.

sentences.note: **next thing it's four o'clock** 은 정신 차려 보니 벌써 네 시더라는 말입니다. 영상을 트는 건 **put on** 을 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 장 본 거 두 봉지에 60달러 나왔어. 고기는 사지도 않았는데. 계산이 잘못된 것 같아서 영수증을 자꾸 들여다보고 있어.
sentences.text: Two bags of groceries was sixty bucks, and I didn't even buy meat. I keep checking the receipt like they made a mistake.

alts.text: Sixty bucks for two bags of groceries, and I didn't even get meat. I keep looking at the receipt like somebody messed up.
Two bags of groceries came to sixty dollars, and I did not even purchase meat. I keep reviewing the receipt as though an error had been made.

sentences.note: **bucks** 는 달러를 편하게 부르는 말입니다. **messed up** 은 누가 실수했다는 뜻으로, 격식을 차리면 **made a mistake** 가 됩니다.

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "how to withdraw that" 은 말을 물린다는 뜻으로 원어민이 쓰지 않는 표현이라 "how to retract that" 으로 고쳤습니다. (withdraw 는 지원서·제안을 공식적으로 거둬들일 때 쓰고, 이미 한 말을 되돌릴 때는 retract 입니다.)
